size: Head and body 45–90 cm · tail 30–55 cm · 3–14 kg

exhibit.habitat: Forest, tundra, prairie, desert and farmland from sea level to 4,500 m — and, more and more, towns. In New Jersey it hunts lawns, parks and golf courses that border wild ground.
exhibit.diet: Mostly rodents — in New Jersey, meadow voles make up about half of what it eats for much of the year — plus rabbits, birds and eggs, insects, berries, carrion and garbage. Extra food is buried in caches and dug up later.
exhibit.distribution: Across the Northern Hemisphere, from the Arctic Circle to Central America, central Asia and North Africa. People introduced it to Australia and the Falkland Islands.
facts: In a Czech study of nearly 600 mouse-hunting pounces, foxes leaping roughly north-east caught their prey 73% of the time, against 18% in most other directions. One idea is that they sense Earth's magnetic field. It is still unproven.
